 Enes Ünal relishes ‘second chance’ with Turkey ahead of starting berth against Belgium
 By Emre Sarigul - November 12, 2026 
 Facebook X 
 Getafe striker Enes Ünal has hailed his return to the Turkish national team as a “career peak,” describing his recall under new manager Sergen Yalçın as a second chance following three injury-plagued years.
 The 29-year-old forward, who has enjoyed a sharp resurgence in La Liga this season, is set to start up front when Turkey host Belgium at İzmir’s Gürsel Aksel Stadium in UEFA Nations League A action on Thursday evening.
 Speaking at his pre-match press conference, Ünal reflected candidly on the physical and psychological toll of prolonged absences from the international setup.
 “I never gave up fighting. I had ups and downs and suffered injuries, which are the worst-case scenario for any professional athlete—a lonely and depressing experience,” Ünal said. “Sitting here today at 29, proud to be back in the national team, feels like a career peak. After the injuries I endured over the last three years, I feel football has given me a second chance.” 
 Ünal also addressed his omission during the latter stages of former manager Vincenzo Montella’s tenure, insisting there was no friction behind the scenes despite his desire to return sooner.
 “We always maintained strong communication with Montella. He wanted to play a very different tactical system and perhaps felt I wasn’t fully ready after coming back from injury. I respect his decision,” Ünal explained. “Now Sergen is our leader, and if given the opportunity tomorrow, I will give everything on the pitch to help turn things around.”
